paper.title_en: Strong gravitational lensing by charged Kalb-Ramond black holes with two nonminimal couplings
paper.abstract_en: We study strong gravitational lensing by the exact static, spherically symmetric electrically charged black-hole solution obtained in a Lorentz-violating Kalb-Ramond background with two independent nonminimal curvature couplings. The space-time solution is used in the form given by the source theory, without introducing a different metric model. Starting from null geodesics, we obtain analytical expressions for the unstable photon orbit and critical impact parameter and derive the logarithmic strong-deflection coefficients. The regular part of the bending integral can be written analytically, while the full deflection integral is also evaluated numerically in order to determine where the strong-deflection approximation is reliable. We then calculate the conventional relativistic-image quantities, including the limiting angular position, angular separation, relative magnification, and the leading winding-time-delay scale. Because the space-time is asymptotically non-Minkowskian, these image quantities are presented as Bozza-type coordinate-winding proxies rather than as a complete global conical-lens reconstruction. Broad values of the Lorentz-violating couplings are used only to display the mathematical response of the lensing quantities. At the representative scale of order $10^{-10}$ quoted in the source study from earlier Lorentz-violation bounds, the corresponding changes in the strong-lensing quantities are of order $10^{-10}$ or smaller for the examples considered here. Consequently, present horizon-scale observations do not provide a useful direct constraint on these small couplings within this calculation.
